decisions.reason: As a flagship product closely tied to the firm's reusable-packaging direction, management would likely keep it absent clear evidence that results fell well below aspirations, though its niche citrus focus raises some risk.
A foldable large-container line with several models and dedicated visibility in both observed years fits the firm's core business well, so a large firm with slack would likely retain it.
A stackable plastic crate line is central to the firm's packaging offer, and even without strong prominence the strategic fit and low need for drastic problemistic search support keeping it.
This pallet line sits squarely in the firm's established transport-packaging capabilities, so unless its performance clearly missed aspiration levels management would be inclined to continue it.

The drop from a standalone page to a simple mention suggests results may have disappointed relative to aspirations, but it still fits the pallet portfolio closely enough that a large firm may keep it for now.

Its reduced prominence after launch points to possible underperformance, yet as a closely related pallet variant with limited additional resource demands it is still somewhat more likely to be retained than dropped.
